tasks.instruction: Read the text below. Choose the correct answer A, B or C for each question.
tasks.text:
A LETTER FROM EDINBURGH

Dear Marta,

I promised I would write properly rather than just sending photographs, so here it is.

We arrived on Thursday, and my first impression was that the city is built on hills that nobody had warned me about. Our flat is at the bottom of one and everything worth seeing is at the top. By Saturday my legs had stopped complaining, which I am told is the local rite of passage.

The castle sits on a rock that was once a volcano, which explains both why it was so hard to attack and why it is so exhausting to walk up to. From the walls you can see the whole city and, on a clear day, the water beyond it. Our guide was a woman of about seventy who told the history of four centuries without once looking at a note, and who clearly enjoyed the grislier parts most.

Running downhill from the castle is a street called the Royal Mile, which ends at the palace where the King stays when he is in Scotland. It is beautiful, and it is also completely full of shops selling the same tartan scarf. Mum bought three of them.

The part I did not expect to like was Arthur's Seat, a hill in the middle of the city which is also an old volcano. You can walk up it in an hour in ordinary shoes. We went early, before the crowds, and at the top there was a wind strong enough to lean on. I have never seen a city look so small from inside itself.

We are here in August, which I now realise was either very clever or a serious mistake. The whole place is taken over by a festival: there are performances in theatres, in pubs, in church halls and, twice that I saw, on the pavement. Anybody at all can take part, which means the quality ranges from genuinely excellent to unwatchable, occasionally within the same show. We saw four things. Two were wonderful. I am choosing not to describe the other two.

One more thing. There is a small statue of a dog near a churchyard, and the story attached to it is that he waited by his owner's grave for years after the owner died. Half the guidebooks say it is true and half say it has been improved over time. I have decided not to look it up, because I prefer it the way the guide told it.

Come with us next time. Bring better shoes than I did.

Love,
Zofia

items.stem: What does Zofia mean by 'the local rite of passage'?
options: A) A ceremony that visitors to the city attend.
B) Getting used to the hills is something every newcomer goes through.
C) A particular walking route through the old town.

items.stem: Why was the castle hard to attack?
options: A) Its walls were unusually thick.
B) It stands on a steep rock.
C) It cannot be seen from the city.

items.stem: What is Zofia's opinion of the Royal Mile?
options: A) Beautiful, but the shops all sell the same thing.
B) Disappointing and not worth the walk.
C) The best part of the whole trip.

items.stem: What surprised Zofia about Arthur's Seat?
options: A) That it is an old volcano.
B) How much she enjoyed it.
C) That climbing it takes a whole day.

items.stem: What does she say about the festival performances?
options: A) They are all of a high standard.
B) Only professional performers may take part.

items.stem: Why has she decided not to check the story about the dog?
options: A) She is certain it is untrue.
B) She would rather keep the version she was told.
C) The guidebooks disagree too much to be any use.
